content:
Laredo ISD is closing out October by celebrating its students: four October Students of the Month, champions honored from four campuses, and 26 elementary students inducted into the National Elementary Honor Society.

The district's October 2026 Students of the Month, announced October 15, are James Peryam of Christen Middle School, Natalia Martinez of Memorial Middle School, Yahir Quinto of Garcia Early College High School, and Rochelle Gonzalez of Martin High School. The Student of the Month program is sponsored by Laredo Federal Credit Union, Clear Choice ER, Chick-Fil-A Marketplace on Bob Bullock, and Laredo Orthodontics.

LISD also celebrated its October Champion Awards Ceremony at Cigarroa High School, recognizing outstanding students from Cigarroa, Nixon and Martin high schools, as well as The RISE Academy, for their achievements, dedication and hard work.

At Milton Elementary School, 26 fourth- and fifth-grade students were inducted into the school's National Elementary Honor Society during a ceremony in the school library. The students were recognized for excellence in the society's four pillars — scholarship, responsibility, service and leadership — and each received a certificate and a medal.

On the field, Martin High School student Angel Valdez was named KGNS Player of the Week after what the district called a record-breaking performance.

The LISD Board of Trustees also used its October 16 special called meeting to approve two commemorative dedications: the football field at M.B. Lamar Middle School will be named in memory of Roque Vela Sr., and the theater at the Vidal M. Treviño School of Communications and Fine Arts will be named and dedicated in memory of Maria Eugenia "Jeanie" Lopez.

Why it matters

October is the month schools ask students to show up — for attendance drives, honor rolls and fall activities — and LISD's calendar shows the district using the same month to name the students who did. The sponsors behind the Student of the Month program, all local businesses, are part of the story too: the recognition runs on community backing, not just campus walls.
